findings.title: Rendered origin is not bound to the issued workspace root
findings.counterexample: With a genuine workspace production lease and genuine fixed producer, supply base of another local folder serving a valid different film.html with the same relative names. Upstream draws base/film.html but stamps and writes under the issued root; loaded URL names are translated to relative names and then identities are read from that root. All PRE/POST identities can remain unchanged and all output digests match the actual wrong-origin draw, so issuer-bound production can activate a witness whose claimed dependencies did not supply the rendered bytes. No exploit was executed.
findings.assertion_gap: B0-1 and B0-4 always call localFolderServer(f.workspaceRoot); the binding is arranged by the fixture, never enforced by production. Producer branding proves executable identity, not which folder answered HTTP.
findings.minimum_same_scope_fix: Bind the permitted rendering origin to the same issued folder/root using Host-private existing serving ownership, and refuse an unrelated or forged origin before the producer runs; add one actual different-folder origin negative. No public DTO, EnginePort, pin or artifact change is requested.

findings.title: Film duration cache still accepts an unwitnessed finite forgery
findings.counterexample: In a stable issued workspace write .film/cache/film-duration.json with film equal to the real film mtime_ms:bytes and duration:999999 (or a negative finite number), without invoking the producer. Classifier returns at1235: no issued witness, actual producer output identity, or duration pairing is consulted. The whole-tree retention detects later mutation but the next stable read accepts these original forged bytes.
findings.assertion_gap: The R04 forged-cache negative targets probe JSON; B0-1 proves pageframe/poster pairing, not duration provenance. Existing finite-number/matching stamp guards reject malformed or stale JSON while allowing a fresh plausible forgery.
findings.minimum_same_scope_fix: Cover this already listed pageframes output with the same real production/identity pairing (including its exact duration cache output when present), or refuse an unwitnessed duration cache. Preserve actual producer positive behavior; do not use the cache as independent duration evidence. Add separate forged-duration and actual-produced stable-round assertions. CONTRACTS_AND_OWNERSHIP.md:42 explicitly includes film-duration.json in the fixed-producer pairing policy; media posters/frames/waves have a different intentionally non-authority policy at41 and are not defects raised here.

findings.title: Cache wrapper PRE/POST multi-failure settlement remains unproven
findings.counterexample: K05-a closes the producer before invocation, so it never acquires POST. K05-b succeeds but throws only for opened[0] and asserts exactly one hit. An implementation that silently lost after.release failures or retained only one of multiple PRE/POST failures would pass these cache cases; the pure retained-closure three-cause case does not execute the wrapper merge/revoke path. This is an oracle counterexample, not a claimed production failure or executed mutation.
findings.assertion_gap: ROUND3_K01_K06_CORRECTIVE_RELEASE_021.md K05 expressly requires original producer error plus PRE/POST cleanup faults and multiple cleanup failures. Current wrapper control flow appears to all-attempt both releases, but the required conjunction is not established by the recorded tests.
findings.minimum_same_scope_fix: Extend the existing Host-private production descriptor seam with named allocation identities from PRE and POST and independent release errors, assert each exact genuine object once, primary preserved, all allocations attempted, no visible witness and sticky refusal. Retain current successful production and single-fault cases; only affected evidence needs re-verification after an authorized fix.
